# MyPyStub

**This cross-platform app was generated by [Briefcase](https://briefcase.readthedocs.io/) - part of [The BeeWare Project](https://beeware.org/). If you want to see more tools like Briefcase, please consider [becoming a financial member of BeeWare](https://beeware.org/contributing/membership).**

My first application for prototyping with iDevices and Python

This application is only tested on iPhone and iPad. It uses the iOS limited subset of *Toga*. It is intended to act as a stub to enable you to install an up-to-date Python interpreter to your device for free. (Apple allows any account to become a Developer account for free that can install up to three apps that are re-deployed once every seven days.)

If you compile and deploy this app, it will create a "MyPyStub" folder in your Files app under "On My iPhone" (or "On My iPad").

You may place Python scripts in there. Either place bare scripts, or place modules in folders. Modules should have a `pyproject.toml` file to nominate any pure-Python dependencies that will attempt to be downloaded from PyPI at runtime.

Only a minimum of packages are preinstalled (if you build this yourself you can pre-install packages by adjusting the *Briefcase* configuration).

## Writing prototypes

The launcher lists your scripts and project folders; tap one to run it. *This lets one of your three free app slots hold many Python prototypes.* Scripts run as they would with `python script.py`, so the same file also works on a desktop, or as a standalone app built with *Briefcase*. Put their start-up code under `if __name__ == "__main__":`.

| Mode | When the run ends | Example |
|---|---|---|
| Plain script (`print`, `input`) | when the script returns | `basics/hello_world.py`, `basics/hello_you.py` |
| Long-running script | when its work finishes | `threads/countdown.py` |
| Main-thread work | when the script returns | `threads/main_thread.py` |
| Arguments and environment variables (set by swiping right for **Setup**) | when the script returns | `basics/args_and_env.py`, `basics/show_args.py`, `basics/show_env.py` |
| Dependencies (PEP 723) | installed first, then as above | `basics/with_dependency.py` |
| Project folder (`pyproject.toml`) | as for its entry point | `basics/hello_project/` |
| Entry points (`[project.scripts]`, `gui-scripts`, other groups) | as for a script; several open like a folder | `projects/two_tools/` |
| Taking over the screen with Toga | when it hands the screen back | `takeover/back_button.py`, `takeover/nested_takeover.py` |

Swipe left on a row for **Info** (a folder's README; a script's docstring, dependencies and source; a project's metadata, README, licence and changelog), and right for **Setup**, which sets its arguments and environment variables, saving as you go. Variables set on the Setup tab's **Environment** page are inherited by every run. The in-app Help page explains each one (see "How your script is run"), and the examples are in the app's **Examples** category. Your own modules are reloaded on each run, so edits take effect without restarting the app.

If you use the special name of `patch_app.py` for your shim you will bypass the Launcher. This is intended if you want to have either a single app and save a tap, or if you need full control of the *Toga* startup.

This is purely experimental at this stage but you're welcome to experiment with it!

## Development

Desktop development uses [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/):

```bash
uv sync
```

```bash
uv run pre-commit install
```

The pre-commit hooks run the same checks as the pull request gate (`.github/workflows/pr-gate.yml`): `ruff check`, `pyright`, and `pytest`. To run them by hand:

```bash
uv run pre-commit run --all-files
```

## Releasing to TestFlight

Builds are shipped by hand from a clone on a Mac with Xcode, Ruby, and Bundler. The `Continuous Delivery to TestFlight` workflow no longer runs on push; it can still be started manually, but only works on a runner that has the credentials below.

```bash
bundle install
```

Export the App Store Connect API key and team details (keep these out of the repository):

- `APP_STORE_CONNECT_KEY_ID`
- `APP_STORE_CONNECT_ISSUER_ID`
- `APP_STORE_CONNECT_PRIVATE_KEY`
- `APP_STORE_TEAM_ID`

Then run one of the lanes in `fastlane/Fastfile`:

```bash
bundle exec fastlane ios share
```

- `share` builds and uploads to TestFlight.
- `local` builds and installs on local devices.
- `manual` builds the Xcode project and leaves signing and deploying to Xcode.

The `share` lane also collects the change fragments in `changes/` into the app's Help → What's New page and commits them (see `changes/README.md`).

Fastlane sets the version, so do not edit it by hand. Before Briefcase runs, it picks today's date and the next build number on TestFlight, and `scripts/set_version.py` stamps them into `pyproject.toml` (restored afterwards). Python sees the build number as a fourth number, so the version is plain PEP 440 with no words. Xcode's version keys hold at most three numbers, so it keeps the build number apart. Every lane numbers its build the same way:

| | Example |
|---|---|
| Python (`app.version`, About page) | `2026.11.2.3` |
| Xcode `CFBundleShortVersionString` | `2026.11.2` |
| Xcode `CFBundleVersion` | `3` |

Runs straight from the source tree (`briefcase dev`, tests) show the placeholder version in `pyproject.toml`.
